title: Quenched Sour Middle Eastern Black Pudding Shawarma Fatteh
description: A festive and flavorful Middle Eastern dish featuring black pudding, a tangy braise, and a crunchy tahini topping.
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the black pudding and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until crispy and golden brown.
Transfer the black pudding to a plate, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, ginger, garlic, and salt to the skillet and stir for 1 minute, releasing the flavors.
Add the pomegranate molasses, apple cider vinegar, and 1 cup water to the skillet and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 5-7 minutes, or until the liquid has thickened slightly and the black pudding is coated.
While the black pudding is browning, toast the pine nuts in a small skillet over medium heat, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly browned.
Stir the toasted pine nuts into the black pudding mixture and cook for 1 minute more.
Fluff the parsley and cilantro with a fork and sprinkle over the black pudding mixture.
Drizzle the tahini over the top and serve immediately on a hot stone plate, garnished with additional parsley and cilantro if desired.
Serve the fatteh hot, garnished with a sprinkle of sumac or paprika, if desired.
Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
